experiments.title: Passive Transfer in a Two-Link Chain
experiments.purpose: Separate work done by applied joint torque from redistribution associated with configuration-dependent inertial coupling.
experiments.hypothesis: With matched initial state and proximal drive, changing distal torque changes when energy is retained proximally and when distal angular speed rises.
experiments.falsifier: The proposed mechanism is challenged if the matched runs show no repeatable change in the distal energy ledger, wrist-interface power, or clubhead-speed timing beyond numerical tolerance.
workflow: Load the passive-transfer preset and run the baseline.
Enable force vectors, moment-of-force arrows, and the energy plots.
Change only the wrist-torque program and rerun.
Compare applied power, segment energy, and clubhead speed at matched times.
tips: A negative wrist torque does not imply negative club acceleration at every instant.
Inspect power and work as well as torque because transfer is configuration and velocity dependent.
limitations: The two-link model omits bilateral hand forces, shaft flexibility, and three-dimensional motion.
A timing association is not by itself evidence of a unique causal pathway.

experiments.title: Distal-Torque Onset Sensitivity
experiments.purpose: Test whether a delayed distal-torque program changes the timing and magnitude of distal speed under bounded inputs.
experiments.hypothesis: Within a bounded family of matched programs, later distal-torque onset can retain energy proximally longer and shift distal acceleration later.
experiments.falsifier: The claim is weakened if onset changes do not survive parameter perturbation, disappear under matched-work comparisons, or reduce clubhead speed across the declared range.
workflow: Select two bounded wrist-torque onset times.
Keep the proximal program and all physical parameters fixed.
Run both cases and overlay wrist torque, wrist power, and clubhead speed.
Repeat with the robustness experiment before generalizing.
tips: Compare both matched peak torque and matched actuator work.
Record the parameter range; an optimum in one range is not a universal strategy.
limitations: The prescribed torque family is a modeling choice rather than a measured neuromuscular command.
Impact, grip compliance, and strength-speed limits are outside this experiment.

experiments.title: Three-Link Transfer Cascade
experiments.purpose: Examine how an additional proximal joint changes the sequence of segment speeds, powers, and energies.
experiments.hypothesis: Staged proximal and middle-joint drive produces a configuration-dependent cascade rather than a fixed one-way packet of energy.
experiments.falsifier: A strict cascade interpretation is challenged when timing order changes without the predicted power-flow signatures or when distal speed is explained entirely by direct distal work.
workflow: Run the staged three-link preset.
Overlay all joint torques, joint powers, and segment angular speeds.
Advance and delay the middle-joint program while holding other inputs fixed.
Inspect whether speed ordering and energy changes remain coupled.
tips: Peak-speed order is a kinematic observation, not a complete energy-transfer measure.
Use the mass-matrix view to see how geometric coupling changes through the motion.
limitations: The open chain does not represent the bilateral closed-loop geometry of two hands on a club.
Segment definitions affect the apparent kinematic sequence.

experiments.title: Two-Hand Force and Equivalent-Couple Mechanism
experiments.purpose: Resolve bilateral hand action into net force and an equivalent couple, then relate that action to club angular acceleration and constraint forces.
experiments.hypothesis: Opposing hand-force components can produce a club couple and late negative club torque without requiring the same net-force direction or a separately prescribed wrist-torque pulse.
experiments.falsifier: The mechanism is challenged if the reconstructed net-force-plus-couple action fails moment equivalence, if the late negative contribution is not robust to admissible geometry changes, or if it is dominated by an unreported applied torque.
workflow: Load the 8-DOF golfer model and project the initial state onto the constraint manifold.
Enable hand-force, net-force, couple, and zero-torque overlays.
Run the bilateral push-pull preset and inspect the late downswing frame by frame.
Compare overall, ZTCF, and DELTA decompositions at the same configuration.
tips: Equal and opposite hand forces can have near-zero net force while retaining a nonzero couple.
Check constraint residuals before interpreting force magnitudes.
limitations: The planar closed-loop model simplifies scapular, wrist, grip, and shaft mechanics.
Constraint forces depend on model geometry and the chosen generalized coordinates.

experiments.title: Pointwise and Forward Zero-Torque Counterfactuals
experiments.purpose: Distinguish an instantaneous zero-applied-torque diagnostic from a trajectory recomputed under a changed torque program.
experiments.hypothesis: Pointwise ZTCF identifies the acceleration or reaction-force tendency at the observed state, while a forward counterfactual can diverge because state and geometry evolve.
experiments.falsifier: The interpretation is challenged if the implementation does not reproduce the declared state, torque removal, sign convention, and constraint treatment or if pointwise and forward results are presented as interchangeable.
workflow: Pause at a selected frame and display the pointwise ZTCF vectors.
Record the state, applied torques, and constraint residual.
Run the forward zero-torque comparator from that state.
Compare only quantities with identical definitions and coordinate conventions.
tips: Pointwise ZTCF answers a local question; it is not a full alternative swing.
A forward counterfactual must recompute the state trajectory and constraint forces.
limitations: Removing modeled torque is not equivalent to removing all muscle action or stiffness.
Counterfactual conclusions remain conditional on model structure and initial state.

experiments.title: Parameter Robustness and Falsifiability Envelope
experiments.purpose: Test whether a reported mechanism survives bounded variation in inertial, geometric, damping, and input parameters.
experiments.hypothesis: A useful mechanism should retain its directional prediction over a declared neighborhood rather than only at one tuned parameter set.
experiments.falsifier: The proposed generalization is rejected outside the subset where its sign, timing, and effect-size criteria remain satisfied with acceptable numerical residuals.
workflow: Choose the baseline transfer experiment and declare parameter bounds.
Run the perturbation analysis with a recorded random seed.
Plot the distribution of effect size and the fraction matching the prediction.
Export failures as well as successes for inspection.
tips: Do not hide sign reversals behind an average effect.
Separate numerical failures from scientifically adverse results.
limitations: A local parameter envelope does not establish population-level biomechanics.
Input distributions are assumptions and must be reported with the result.

glossary.definition: A generalized moment supplied explicitly by the model input at a joint.
glossary.plain_language: The turning input commanded at a modeled joint.
glossary.caution: It is not the same as the total moment acting on a segment.

glossary.definition: The portion of a joint-level dynamic balance associated with motion-dependent coupling among modeled coordinates.
glossary.plain_language: Turning tendency that appears because the linked system is moving and changing geometry.
glossary.caution: Its numerical value depends on the coordinate convention and decomposition.

glossary.definition: A reaction force or generalized force required to satisfy the model's kinematic constraints.
glossary.plain_language: The force needed to keep the two-hand loop closed in the model.
glossary.caution: Large values can reflect poor constraint conditioning or an inconsistent state.

glossary.definition: The free moment that, together with a resultant force at a chosen point, reproduces the moment of a distributed force system.
glossary.plain_language: The residual twist left after two hand forces are replaced by one net force.
glossary.caution: The net force's moment depends on the selected reduction point; the complete wrench must be compared.

glossary.definition: A new trajectory integrated after changing an input or model condition from a declared initial state.
glossary.plain_language: Rerun the model after changing one rule and let the motion evolve differently.
glossary.caution: It answers a different question from a pointwise diagnostic.

glossary.definition: A coordinate used to parameterize the model configuration, such as a joint angle.
glossary.plain_language: One of the numbers used to describe the model's pose.
glossary.caution: Coordinate choices affect component-wise decompositions but not the underlying physical motion.

glossary.definition: Configuration-dependent off-diagonal terms in the mass matrix that couple generalized accelerations and forces.
glossary.plain_language: Acceleration of one link changes the effort and response of another linked part.
glossary.caution: Coupling permits redistribution but does not by itself identify a one-way energy source.

glossary.definition: A matrix mapping generalized velocities to a selected task-space velocity, with a transpose relation for forces.
glossary.plain_language: A geometry map between joint motion and point motion or force.
glossary.caution: Near singular configurations, inversion can be ill-conditioned.

glossary.definition: The observed ordering of selected segment or joint velocity peaks.
glossary.plain_language: Which modeled part reaches its peak speed first, second, and so on.
glossary.caution: Peak order alone does not quantify energy transfer or causation.

glossary.definition: The configuration-dependent matrix relating generalized acceleration to the inertial portion of generalized force.
glossary.plain_language: The pose-dependent inertia map of the linked system.
glossary.caution: Off-diagonal terms depend on the generalized-coordinate definition.

glossary.definition: The rotational tendency produced by a force about a declared point or axis.
glossary.plain_language: Force multiplied by its perpendicular leverage about a point.
glossary.caution: Always report the point, axis, and sign convention.

glossary.definition: The instantaneous rate of mechanical work; at a revolute joint it is torque multiplied by angular velocity under a consistent sign convention.
glossary.plain_language: How quickly a modeled action adds or removes mechanical energy.
glossary.caution: Torque sign alone does not determine power sign.

glossary.definition: Relative anatomical or model locations nearer to and farther from the chain's chosen base.
glossary.plain_language: Closer to the body versus farther along the linked chain.
glossary.caution: The labels describe location, not a guaranteed direction of transfer.

glossary.definition: A loss or reduction of effective load transmission caused by compliance, clearance, changing contact, or low tension, which must be defined for the specific model or measurement.
glossary.plain_language: A condition where motion or force is not transmitted immediately through the intended path.
glossary.caution: A rigid-link model cannot establish physiological slack without an explicit compliance or contact state.

glossary.definition: Power transferred across the modeled hand-club interface under a declared force, moment, velocity, and sign convention.
glossary.plain_language: The instantaneous energy rate crossing between the hands and club in the model.
glossary.caution: Different segment and interface conventions can change the reported component signs.

glossary.definition: The time integral of mechanical power over a declared interval.
glossary.plain_language: Accumulated mechanical energy added or removed during part of the motion.
glossary.caution: The integration interval and sign convention must accompany the value.

glossary.definition: A pointwise diagnostic force or acceleration computed at a specified state after setting declared applied torques to zero while retaining the stated model terms.
glossary.plain_language: What the model predicts locally if the selected commanded torques are removed at this exact state.
glossary.caution: ZTCF is a local counterfactual, not automatically a forward no-torque trajectory or a muscle-off condition.
